<meta>continues from previous page: the root verse 56 completes the description of the Sītkārī breath-retention begun on the previous page</meta>

**Root text** <note>original: "mū°", short for <term>mūla</term> <gloss>the root verses of Svātmārāma, as distinct from the commentary</gloss></note> . . . and strength of body arises, free from every affliction.
By this method, truly, he becomes a lord among yogis on the face of the earth. ॥ 56 ॥

### Now the Śītalī ॥ <note><term>Śītalī</term> <gloss>"the cooling one"</gloss>, a breath-retention practised by drawing air in over the tongue.</note>

Drawing in the air with the tongue, let the wise one perform the breath-retention as before,
and then slowly expel the breath through the two nostrils. ॥ 57 ॥

Abdominal swellings, disorders of the spleen and other diseases, fever, bile, hunger and thirst,
and poisons: this breath-retention called Śītalī destroys them all. ॥ 58 ॥

---

->॥ Commentary ॥<- <note>This is the Sanskrit commentary printed with the root text, generally identified as Brahmānanda's <term>Jyotsnā</term> <gloss>"Moonlight"</gloss>.</note>

"Bhavet" ॥ Strength <note>original: "sattvam", glossed as "balam", strength</note> of the body <note>"dehasya" glossed as "śarīrasya"</note> also arises. By this method just stated, that is, the method of practice, the lord of yogis, meaning one who is like Indra among yogis, becomes truly free from all afflictions on the face of the earth. Following the maxim "every statement carries an emphasis" <note>original: "sarvaṃ vākyaṃ sāvadhāraṇam"</note>, the meaning is that the fruit which has been stated is indeed true. ॥ 56 ॥

He now describes the Śītalī breath-retention ॥ "Jihvayā" <note>"with the tongue"</note>. With the tongue put out beyond the lips, shaped like the lower half of a bird's beak, drawing in the air: the meaning is "having slowly made the inhalation" <note><term>pūraka</term> <gloss>the in-breath</gloss></note>. "As before" means as in the Sūryabhedana: the words "having carried out the performance of the retention" <note><term>kumbha</term>, that is <term>kumbhaka</term> <gloss>holding of the breath</gloss></note> are to be supplied. "The wise one": one whose understanding is excellent. Through the two openings of the nose, that is, through the cavities of the nostrils, "śanakaiḥ", meaning simply "slowly". <note>The commentator explains the grammar: by Pāṇini's rule beginning "avyaya-sarvanāmnām", the suffix <term>akac</term> is inserted into the adverb "śanaiḥ", giving the form "śanakaiḥ" with the same meaning.</note> Let him expel <note><term>recaka</term> <gloss>the out-breath</gloss></note> the breath, that is, the air. ॥ 57 ॥

He states the benefits of the Śītalī ॥ "Gulma". Gulma and plīha, abdominal swelling and disease of the spleen, are particular diseases; those disorders which begin with these two are "gulma, plīha and the rest". Fever: the disease called fever. Bile: disorders of the bile. Hunger: the desire to eat. Thirst: the desire to drink water. Poisons: the disorders produced by the venom of snakes and the like. "Called Śītalī" <note>original: "śītalī-nāma"</note>: here "nāma" is an indeclinable carrying the sense "well known as". This breath-retention just described "nihanti", destroys, that is, destroys utterly. The word "kumbha" in the femin- <note>The sentence breaks off at the foot of the page; the commentator is explaining why the feminine form "kumbhikā" is used.</note>

---

->॥ Vernacular explanation ॥<- <note>original: "bhāṣā", a paraphrase in the Hindi of the period, printed beneath the Sanskrit commentary</note>

"Bhavet" ॥ Strength comes to the body, and by this method of practice that has been described, one who is like Indra among yogis becomes free from all afflictions on the earth. The fruit that has been stated here is true. ॥ 56 ॥

Now we describe the fourth, the Śītalī breath-retention ॥ "Jihvayā". Putting one's tongue out beyond the lips like the lower half of a bird's beak, drawing in the air and making the inhalation, one should then carry out the breath-retention just as was described earlier for the Sūryabhedana. Then he whose understanding is fine should slowly, slowly expel the air through the openings of the nose. ॥ 57 ॥

We describe the benefits of the Śītalī ॥ "Gulma". Abdominal swelling and disease of the spleen, and the diseases that begin with these; and fever, and disorders of the bile; and the desire to eat, the desire to drink water; and the venom of snakebite and other poisons as well: all these the breath-retention named Śītalī removes. ॥ 58 ॥

<summary>This page of the Haṭhayogapradīpikā (verses 2.56 to 2.58) closes the account of the Sītkārī breath-retention and teaches the Śītalī, in which air is drawn in over a protruding tongue, held, and released through the nose. It lists the ailments Śītalī is said to cure, with a Sanskrit commentary and a Hindi paraphrase explaining each word.</summary>
